newsitem.title: UK: Brittania buys Scotam's third party funds business.
newsitem.headline: Brittania buys Scotam's third party funds business.

text.p: Britannia Investment Managers said on Monday it had bought Scottish Amicable Investment Managers' third party institutional funds business for an undisclosed sum.
The acquisition follows the decision by insurance giant Prudential Corp Plc to transfer the management of its Scottish Amicable policyholder funds to London from Glasgow.
It said the acquisition would raise total funds under management at the Glasgow-based investment management company to 5.3 billion sterling from 4.5 billion.
BIM managing director Danny O'Neill said the deal would give it critical mass, a presence in the segregated market and a foothold in the investment trust business.
It is expected to be completed in September after a period of due diligence investigations.
BIM and Britannia Fund Managers are the investment management and unit trust subsidiaries of Britannia Building Society.
He said the retention of the third party business in Scotland was positive for the region's investment community.
Douglas Ferrens, SAIM chief executive, will move to BIM as marketing director along with 16 other SAIM employees.
